meta.name: rule_help
meta.description: 218 (plan G-process-core P3e, the owner's request and decisions of 2026-10-23): the plain-language description of the rules for the read-only view in Settings › Rules. For every machine decision point of the decision trace (jav/core/trace.py): its area, a short title, what it decides and what it is not for, and the rule values the view shows (file, key, label, format; a percentage's label reads on into its value, as in 'below 60 %'); the values themselves are read from the rule files the running process loaded (jav/app/rules_view.py). Kept apart from the rule files, so their fingerprints and the AI requests do not change. Texts are English; the interface translates them (ui/src/i18n/hu-native.json). A test asks that every decision point has an entry and that every value's key is in a file its point reads.

changelog.note: 231 (stage D, D-c2, D-c3): the product registry's two decision points (a product rule's outcome on an assessed unit, a premium from a tariff), their area and the fact catalogues they read.
231 (plan stage B, B3): the quotes' two decision points (an approved quote's totals, the check of the model's letter paragraph), their area and their rule files.

224 (plan G-process-core P3c): the values follow the split of the shared rule file - the email routes from email.json, the duplicate search from finance.json; their titles. Only the file and the key of a shown value changed, not its label.
218 (P3e): first version - the ten decision points of the decision trace, in five areas, with their rule values and the titles of the rule files they read.

finance.duplicate.title: Duplicate invoice
finance.duplicate.what: Whether an invoice is the same invoice as another one in the store (the same kind, number and supplier), and of which kind: an exact copy, a modified version, or undecidable because a field is missing.
finance.duplicate.not_for: A person's decision on the pair, or how the totals count a confirmed copy.

parties.own_tax_as_supplier.what: Whether an incoming invoice names an own party's tax number as the supplier's while the buyer's is another number or missing: the numbers are likely swapped, or it is an outgoing invoice.
parties.own_tax_as_supplier.not_for: The same number on both sides (another check), or the invoice's direction by the own parties.

quote.amounts.title: A quote's totals
quote.amounts.what: An approved quote's net, VAT and gross totals, computed by code from its lines' unit prices, quantities and discounts, each line's amount and the VAT rounded to the unit of its currency.
quote.amounts.not_for: The lines' prices and discounts themselves (the price list and a person's own prices), or which item a requested line is.

quote.letter_check.title: The model's letter paragraph
quote.letter_check.what: Whether the paragraph a model wrote for a quote's reply letter can be used: not empty, with no number, amount, date, address or link in it, and not longer than the limit; otherwise the letter waits for a person.
quote.letter_check.not_for: The letter's frame (written by code) or a person's acceptance of the letter.

values.label: Longest paragraph, in characters

rules.outcome.title: A product rule's outcome
rules.outcome.what: What a product rule gives on an assessed unit (a policyholder, a site, an asset group): the first row of its decision table whose comparisons hold on the facts the unit and its parents have (or every such row). A row a missing fact leaves open makes the outcome not known and names the fact; a row false whatever the missing facts are is skipped.
rules.outcome.not_for: How several rules' outcomes combine on a unit (the catalogue's way: the worst verdict, the largest deductible, ...) or a person's decision on the risk.

values.label: Verdicts, the best first

rating.premium.title: A premium from a tariff
rating.premium.what: A quote's premium computed by code from the tariff the case keeps, in a fixed order: each cover module's basis times its rate per thousand and its factors, each line rounded, a module's minimum, the modules summed, the total factors, the total rounded and the policy minimum. A missing factor, a value no row takes, a cover start out of force or another currency gives no total.
rating.premium.not_for: The tariff's rates and factors themselves (Settings › Tariffs) or a person's decision on the premium.

values.label: The levels a tariff prices on
